verses.zh: 有话说：人若休妻，妻离他而去，作了别人的妻，前夫岂能再收回她来？若收回她来，那地岂不是大大玷污了吗？但你和许多亲爱的行邪淫，还可以归向我。这是耶和华说的。
verses.en: “If a man divorces his wifeand she leaves him and becomes another man’s wife,he may not take her back again.[NOTE:1] Doing that would utterly defile the land.[NOTE:2] But you, Israel, have given yourself as a prostitute to many gods.[NOTE:3] So what makes you think you can return to me?”[NOTE:4] says the Lord.
notes: Heb “May he go back to her again?” The question is rhetorical and expects a negative answer.sn For the legal background for the illustration that is used here, see Deut 24:1-4.
Heb “Would the land not be utterly defiled?” The stative is here rendered actively to connect better with the preceding. The question is rhetorical and expects a positive answer.
Heb “But you have played the prostitute with many lovers.”

Heb “Returning to me.” The form is the bare infinitive, which the KJV and ASV have interpreted as an imperative: “Yet, return to me!” However, it is more likely that a question is intended, expressing surprise in the light of the law alluded to and the facts cited. For the use of the infinitive absolute in the place of a finite verb, cf. GKC 346 §113.ee. For the introduction of a question without a question marker, cf. GKC 473 §150.a.
verses.commentary:
3:1

NASB
"God says"

NKJV
"they say"

NRSV, LXX, NJB, REB
—omit—

TEV
"The Lord says"

JPSOA
"[the word of the Lord came to me]

as follows"

The MT simply has the Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT (BDB 55, KB 65)
"saying." The UBS Text Project suggests (p. 180)

- it introduces a principal, a proverb, or judicial statement

- it relates to Jer. 2:37

▣ "If a husband divorces his wife" This reflects Moses' statement in Deut. 24:3-4. YHWH
uses divorce as imagery of His peoples' "spiritual adultery" (i.e. idolatry). Israelites could not
take back a wife after another man had married her (cf. Deut. 24:4), but YHWH's great love will
remarry Israel even after her idolatry (Jer. 4:1; Hosea 1-3).

YHWH was stating what had occurred years ago (see full note at Jer. 2:20-25).

SPECIAL TOPIC: DIVORCE

▣ "Will he still return to her?" This was not allowed (cf. Deut. 24:1-4).

▣ "land be completely polluted" The IMPERFECT VERB and INFINITIVE
ABSOLUTE of the same root (BDB 337, KB 335) are used to intensify the sense of the idolatrous
pollution. This very thing is discussed in Lev. 18:24-28; 19:29; Deut. 24:4.

The LXX (NEB, REB) has "woman," האשׁה, (cf. v. 9), but the MT has
"land," הארץ. The UBS Text Project rates "land" as "B" (some doubt); both
fit the context.

There are three Hebrew roots that denote pollution and defilement.

- BDB 379, KB 375 ‒ pollution by idolatry

- Jer. 2:7; 3:9; 16:18, defile the land

- Jer. 2:23 ‒ Israel's denial of pollution

- BDB 337, KB 335 ‒ polluted by idolatry

- Jer. 3:1,2, defiled the land (Ps. 106:38; Isa. 24:5)

- Jer. 23:11 ‒ prophets and priests polluted (Dan. 11:32)

- BDB 320 II, KB 319 ‒ Jer. 34:16 ‒ pollute the Name of YHWH (cf. Lev. 18:21;
19:12; 20:3; 21:6; 22:2,32; Ezek. 20:39; Amos 2:7

▣ "you are a harlot with many lovers" YHWH is depicted as a husband, possibly
based on Deut. 10:20; 11:22; 13:4 (i.e. "cling to Him"). This is one of several anthropomorphic
metaphors used of God and His relationship to His faith children.

The shocking imagery of covenant Israel as a "harlot" (i.e. spiritual idolatry with
pagan idols) is expanded in the book of Revelation, where, I think, "the great harlot" refers to Jerusalem
and the "red beast" on which she rides, refers to the Roman Empire (cf. Rev. 17). In eschatological
studies, this position is known as Partial Preterism. Please see my new (2024) verse-by-verse
commentary on the book of the Revelation, online at www.freebiblecommentary.org

SPECIAL TOPIC: PROBLEMS AND LIMITATIONS OF HUMAN LANGUAGE

▣

NASB
"Yet you turn to Me"

NKJV
"yet return to Me"

TEV
"now you want to return to Me?"

LXX, NJB
"would you return to me?"

JPSOA
"can you return to Me?"

Peshitta
"return again to me"

This is the INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE of a VERB (Qal
IMPERFECT, BDB 996, KB 1427) used earlier in the verse (and throughout this chapter). This
refers to Israelite worship that had combined the worship of YHWH with pagan worship practices. Its grammatical
form can be

- "turned to," an IMPERATIVE (NKJV)

- "are turned," a VERB (NASB)

- "returned," a question (TEV, NJB, JPSOA following the LXX)

SPECIAL TOPIC: REPENTANCE (OT)

verses.zh: 你向净光的高处举目观看，你在何处没有淫行呢？你坐在道旁等候，好像阿拉伯人在旷野埋伏一样，并且你的淫行邪恶玷污了全地。
verses.en: “Look up at the hilltops and consider this.[NOTE:1] Where have you not been ravished?[NOTE:2] You waited for those gods like a thief lying in wait in the wilderness.[NOTE:3] You defiled the land by your wicked prostitution to other gods.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “and see.”

The rhetorical question expects the answer “nowhere,” which asserts the widespread nature of the nation’s idolatry. The prophets often compare Judah’s religious infidelity, idolatry, to adultery or prostitution. Jeremiah goes a step further in exposing their folly by portraying their willing acts of idolatry as being sexually violated.
Heb “You sat for them [the lovers, i.e., the foreign gods] beside the road like an Arab in the desert.”
Heb “by your prostitution and your wickedness.” This is probably an example of hendiadys where, when two nouns are joined by “and,” one expresses the main idea and the other qualifies it.
verses.commentary:
3:2 "Lift up your eyes. . .see" These are both Qal IMPERATIVES.

- lift up ‒ BDB 669, KB 724

- see ‒ BDB 906, KB 1157, cf. Jer. 1:10; 2:10 (twice), 19, 23, 31

▣ "bare heights" This was the place of the worship of Ba'al and
Asherah (cf. Jer. 3:21; 4:11; 7:29; 12:12; 14:6; Hosea 4:11-14).

SPECIAL TOPIC: FERTILITY WORSHIP OF THE ANE

▣

NASB
"violated"

NKJV
"lain with men"

NJB, JPSOA, REB
"lain with"

TEV
"acted like a prostitute"

LXX
"contaminated" or "utterly defiled"

Peshitta
"defiled yourself"

The MT has "be ravished" (שׁגל, BDB 993, KB 1415, cf. NASB), but
the Masoretic scholars suggest "be lain with" (שׁכב, BDB 1011, KB 1486).

The covenant people were not raped. They voluntarily committed "spiritual adultery"
with foreign idols seeking prosperity and fertility of their families, herds, and crops.

▣ "By the roads you have sat" This is an historical/cultural reference to what the
prostitutes did (cf. Gen. 38:14; Prov. 7:12ff; Ezek. 16:25).

▣

NASB, NRSV, TEV, REB
"Arab"

NKJV
"Arabian"

NJB
"nomad"

JPSOA
"bandit"

Peshitta
"ostrich"

The MT has "Arabian" (ערבי, BDB 787 IV, cf. Isa. 13:20), but
the Septuagint has "raven" (ערב, BDB 788 VI).

The JPSOA interprets the word as a robber (see UBS Handbook, p. 94). The
LXX's "raven" could be parallel to "polluted land," as the raven was an unclean scavenger, but it
could also mean a supposed helper, cf. 1 Kgs. 17:4.

▣ "harlotry" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: FERTILITY WORSHIP OF THE ANE.

verses.zh: 因此甘霖停止，春（原文是晚）雨不降。你还是有娼妓之脸，不顾羞耻。
verses.en: That is why the rains have been withheldand the spring rains have not come.Yet in spite of this you are obstinate as a prostitute.[NOTE:1] You refuse to be ashamed of what you have done.
notes: Heb “you have the forehead of a prostitute.”
verses.commentary:
3:3 The first two lines are poetic parallel. God tried to use the cycles of nature to open the eyes
of His people (cf. Lev. 26:14-20; Deut. 28:15-68), but they would not see. There are two rainy seasons
in Palestine (cf. Deut. 11:14), one at planting time and the other as the plants mature. Most moisture
came from daily dew.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEBREW POETRY

▣ "harlot's forehead" This is a reference either to

- characteristic ornamentation (cf. Rev. 17:5)

- imagery for stubbornness (JPSOA, "brazenness") and lack of shame (cf. Ezek. 3:7-8)

verses.zh: 从今以后，你岂不向我呼叫说：我父啊，你是我幼年的恩主。
verses.en: Even now you say to me, ‘You are my father![NOTE:1] You have been my faithful companion ever since I was young.
notes: Heb “Have you not just now called out to me, ‘[You are] My father!’?” The rhetorical question expects a positive answer.
verses.commentary:
3:4 "My Father" This is another family image for God.

SPECIAL TOPIC: FATHERHOOD OF GOD

verses.zh: 耶和华岂永远怀怒，存留到底吗？看哪，你又发恶言又行坏事，随自己的私意而行（或译：你虽这样说，还是行恶放纵欲心）。
verses.en: You will not always be angry with me, will you?You will not be mad at me forever, will you?’[NOTE:1] That is what you say,but you continually do all the evil that you can.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “Will he keep angry forever? Will he maintain [it] to the end?” The questions are rhetorical and expect a negative answer. The change to direct address in the English translation is intended to ease the problem of the rapid transition, common in Hebrew style (but not in English), from second person direct address in the preceding lines to third person indirect address in these two lines. See GKC 462 §144.p.
Heb “You do the evil and you are able.” This is an example of hendiadys, meaning, “You do all the evil that you are able to do.”
verses.commentary:
3:5 "Will He be angry forever" They were trying to take advantage of God's mercy. This same
concept is discussed in Ps. 103:8-14. God's mercy was not the issue, but their willful and repeated
idolatry (cf. Jer. 3:12-14).

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHARACTERISTICS OF ISRAEL'S GOD (OT)

▣ "angry. . .indignant" The JPSOA footnote asserts that the MT reflects Akkadian parallels
(i.e. "hate" and "rage").

- maintain wrath (BDB 643, #1, KB 695, Qal IMPERFECT), cf. v. 12; Ps. 103:9; Micah 7:18
similar statements)

- indignant ((BDB 1036, KB 1581, Qal IMPERFECT, like #1,
means "retain wrath," cf. Amos 1:11

There is a biblical tension between

- YHWH's forever judgments

- YHWH's willingness to not hold on to His anger

This seems confusing and contradictory to western thinking, but it fits perfectly the eastern mentality
of putting truth to tension filled pairs (i.e. paradox), and thereby seeking humans to purposely remain in the tension.

SPECIAL TOPIC: EASTERN LITERATURE (biblical paradoxes)

▣ "spoken. . .done evil" Their lips said one thing, but their actions showed another
(cf. Jer. 2:20,23-25; Isa. 29:13).

verses.zh: 约西亚王在位的时候，耶和华又对我说：「背道的以色列所行的，你看见没有？她上各高山，在各青翠树下行淫。
verses.en: When Josiah was king of Judah, the Lord said to me, “Jeremiah, you have no doubt seen what wayward Israel has done.[NOTE:1] You have seen how she went up to every high hill and under every green tree to give herself like a prostitute to other gods.[NOTE:2]
notes: “Have you seen…” The question is rhetorical and expects a positive answer.

Heb “she played the prostitute there.” This is a metaphor for Israel’s worship; she gave herself to the worship of other gods like a prostitute gives herself to her lovers. There seems no clear way to completely spell out the metaphor in the translation.
verses.commentary:
3:6 "Then the Lord said to me in the days of Josiah the king" This
surely dates the poem and by implication the surrounding strophes.

For the reign of King Josiah see
SPECIAL TOPIC: KINGS OF THE DIVIDED MONARCHY.

▣ "Israel" These are the northern ten tribes. Jeremiah 3:7-8,10,11 show that in light of
Israel's sin, Judah should have learned, but she did not, and even copied her sister's sins
(cf. Ezek. 16:44-52; 23).

The northern kingdom was known by three titles.

- Israel (a collective term)

- Ephraim (the largest tribe)

- Samaria (the capital city)

▣ "on every high hill and under every green tree" This was the site for Ba'al worship (cf. Deut. 12:7;
1 Kgs. 14:23; 2 Kgs. 16:4; 17:10; 2 Chr. 28:4; Isa. 57:5,7; Jer. 3:2-3,6; 17:2,8; Ezek. 6:13; 20:28; Hosea 4:11-14).

SPECIAL TOPIC: FERTILITY WORSHIP OF THE ANE

verses.zh: 她行这些事以后，我说她必归向我，她却不归向我。她奸诈的妹妹犹大也看见了。
verses.en: Yet even after she had done all that, I thought that she might come back to me.[NOTE:1] But she did not. Her sister, unfaithful Judah, saw what she did.[NOTE:2]
notes: Or “I said to her, ‘Come back to me!’” The verb אָמַר (ʾamar) usually means “to say,” but here it means “to think,” of an assumption that turns out to be wrong (so HALOT 66 s.v. אמר 4) (cf. Gen 44:28; Jer 3:19; Pss 82:6; 139:11; Job 29:18; Ruth 4:4; Lam 3:18).sn Open theists suggest that passages such as this indicate God has limited foreknowledge; however, more traditional theologians view this passage as an extended metaphor in which God presents himself as a deserted husband, hoping against hope that his adulterous wife might return to him. The point of the metaphor is not to make an assertion about God’s foreknowledge, but to develop the theme of God’s heartbreak due to Israel’s unrepentance.
The words “what she did” are not in the text but are implicit from the context and are supplied in the translation for clarification.
verses.commentary:
3:7 "Judah" These are the southern three tribes of Judah, Simeon, and Benjamin. Most of the
Levites and priests also stayed with the southern tribes.

▣ "she will return to Me" The word "return" (BDB 996, KB 1427) is Hebrew imagery
for repentance. It is used several times in this chapter (cf. Jer. 3:1 [twice], 7 [twice], 10, 12,14, 19, 22). The OT, as
the NT, is a conditional covenant as it relates to human choices, but an unconditional covenant as to
YHWH's plan to redeem those individuals who will turn to Him by repentance and faith (cf. Mark 1:15;
Acts 3:16,19; 20:21).

SPECIAL TOPIC: REPENTANCE (OT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: REPENTANCE (NT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

verses.zh: 背道的以色列行淫，我为这缘故给她休书休她；我看见她奸诈的妹妹犹大，还不惧怕，也去行淫。
verses.en: She also saw[NOTE:1] that, because of wayward Israel’s adulterous worship of other gods,[NOTE:2] I sent her away and gave her divorce papers. But still her unfaithful sister Judah was not afraid, and she too went and gave herself like a prostitute to other gods.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “she [‘her sister, unfaithful Judah’ from the preceding verse] saw” with one Hebrew ms, some Greek mss, and the Syriac version. The MT reads, “I saw,” which may be a case of attraction to the verb at the beginning of the previous verse.
Heb “because she committed adultery.” The translation is intended to spell out the significance of the metaphor.

Heb “she played the prostitute there.” This is a metaphor for Israel’s worship; she gave herself to the worship of other gods like a prostitute gives herself to her lovers. There seems no clear way to completely spell out the metaphor in the translation.
verses.commentary:
3:8

NASB, NKJV, LXX
"I saw. . ."

TEV
"Judah also saw. . ."

NRSV
"She also saw. . ."

NJB, REB, Peshitta
"She saw"

JPSOA
"I noted:""

The MT has "and I saw" (וארא), but the DSS, Peshitta, and the Vulgate
versions have "she saw" (ותרא). The UBS Text Project gives the MT a B rating
(some doubt).

The next line describes YHWH's actions in light of Israel's response.

▣ "I had sent her away" This links the Assyrian exile (i.e. 722 B.C.) with the imagery
of divorce ("send away," BDB 1018, KB 1511, Piel PERFECT, cf. Deut. 22:19,29; 24:1,3; Jer. 3:1).

▣ "writ of divorce" This was a legal document first discussed in Deut. 24:1-4.

- involved some legal procedures which took some time so that the couple could work out
their differences if possible

- another person had to be involved (i.e. a Levite)

- involved the restitution of the dowry to the wife or her family

- allowed the vulnerable woman to remarry and be a functioning member of that society

SPECIAL TOPIC: CERTIFICATE OF DIVORCE

▣ "yet her treacherous sister Judah did not fear" Israel is described as "faithless" (BDB 1000) in
vv. 6,8,11,12. This root denotes apostasy from YHWH and His covenant (cf. Jer. 2:19; 3:22; 5:6; 8:5; 14:7; Hosea 6:7).

Judah, seeing what happened to Israel (i.e. exile), still continued down the same path of threachery
(BDB 93, KB 108, Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE), especially in marriage (here, spiritual adultery
with pagan idols, cf. Jer. 3:20; 9:2). For other usages see Isa. 24:16; 33:1; 48:8; Jer. 3:8,10,11; 5:11; 12:1,6; Hosea 5:7).

Ezekiel discusses this same issue of Judah's lack of understanding about the consequenes of
idolatry that fell on the northern tribes (cf. Ezek. 10:44-52; all of chapter 23).

SPECIAL TOPIC: CONSEQUENCES OF IDOLATRY

verses.zh: 因以色列轻忽了她的淫乱，和石头木头行淫，地就被玷污了。
verses.en: Because she took her prostitution so lightly, she defiled the land[NOTE:1] through her adulterous worship of gods made of wood and stone.[NOTE:2]
notes: The translation reads the form as a causative (Hiphil, תַּהֲנֵף, tahanef) with some of the versions in place of the simple stative (Qal, תֶּחֱנַף, tekhenaf) in the MT.
Heb “because of the lightness of her prostitution, she defiled the land and committed adultery with stone and wood.”
verses.commentary:
3:9

NASB
"the lightness of her harlotry"

NKJV
"her casual harlotry"

NRSV
"her shameless whoring"

TEV
"was not at all ashamed"

NJB
"she took her whoredom so lightly"

JPSOA
"her casual immorality"

REB
"her casual prostitution"

LXX
"her whoredom came to nothing"

The key word is "so light" (קל, BDB 887, KB 1101 I), found
only here. BDB suggests "lightness" or "frivolity."

▣ "stones and trees" This is a reference to the male Canaanite deity, Ba'al, symbolized by an
uplifted stone, and the female Canaanite deity, Asherah, symbolized by a live tree or carved tree (cf. Jer. 2:27).
These pagan fertility gods were worshiped in every town, either on a manmade, raised platform of cut stones or on a close by hill.

verses.zh: 虽有这一切的事，她奸诈的妹妹犹大还不一心归向我，不过是假意归我。这是耶和华说的。」
verses.en: In spite of all this,[NOTE:1] Israel’s sister, unfaithful Judah, has not turned back to me with any sincerity; she has only pretended to do so,”[NOTE:2] says the Lord.
notes: Heb “And even in all this.”
Heb “has not turned back to me with all her heart but only in falsehood.”
verses.commentary:
3:10 "Judah did not return to Me with all her heart" This may be a reference to the reforms of
Hezekiah or Josiah. The reforms of these godly kings were only superficially accepted by the populous.

For "returned" see
SPECIAL TOPIC: REPENTANCE (OT).

For "heart" see SPECIAL TOPIC: HEART.

verses.zh: 耶和华对我说：「背道的以色列比奸诈的犹大还显为义。
verses.en: Then the Lord said to me, “Under the circumstances, wayward Israel could even be considered less guilty than unfaithful Judah.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “Wayward Israel has proven herself to be more righteous than unfaithful Judah.”sn A comparison is drawn here between the greater culpability of Judah, who has had the advantage of seeing how God disciplined her sister nation for having sinned and yet ignored the warning and committed the same sin, and the culpability of Israel, who had no such advantage.

verses.zh: 你去向北方宣告说：耶和华说：背道的以色列啊，回来吧！我必不怒目看你们；因为我是慈爱的，我必不永远存怒。这是耶和华说的。
verses.en: “Go and shout this message to my people in the countries in the north.[NOTE:1] Tell them: ‘Come back to me, wayward Israel,’ says the Lord.‘I will not continue to look on you with displeasure.[NOTE:2] For I am merciful,’ says the Lord.‘I will not be angry with you forever.
notes: Heb “Go and proclaim these words to the north.” The translation assumes that the message is directed toward the exiles of northern Israel who have been scattered in the provinces of Assyria to the north.
Heb “I will not cause my face to fall on you.”
verses.commentary:
3:12-14 The NASB, NKJV, NRSV, NJB all show these verses in poetic form (like Jer. 3:1-5 and
Jer. 3:19-20).

- God tells the prophet to

- go (Qal INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE)

- proclaim (Qal PERFECT with waw)

- God tells the northern tribes to

- return (Qal IMPERATIVE, see note at Jer. 3:1)

- acknowledge (lit. "know," Qal IMPERATIVE; see SPECIAL TOPIC: KNOW)

(1) your iniquity

(2) that you have transgressed (Qal PERFECT)

(3) that you scattered your favors (BDB 202) to strangers (i.e. idols)

(4) that you have not obeyed (Qal PERFECT; see SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP)

- If they will obey, God will

- not look upon you in anger

- not be angry forever (see v. 5)

This literary form has been called "a summons to repentance" in Cracking OT Codes by Sandy
and Giese (p. 164). It includes a divine promise, an accusation of sin, and a divine threat of judgment
(cf. Isa. 1:19-20; 55:6-7; Jer. 3:12-13; 4:1-4; Joel 2:12-13; Amos 5:4-7,14-15).

3:12 "For I am gracious" This is one of the primary presuppositions of the character of Deity. Often
in other world religions, deity is capricious, detached, but not so the God of the Bible. Note His repeated
characteristics.

- compassionate (BDB 933), cf. Exod. 34:6; Deut. 4:31; Neh. 9:17; Ps. 86:15; 103:8; 145:8; Joel 2:13

- gracious (BDB 337), cf. Exod. 34:6; Neh. 9:17; Ps. 86:15; 103:8; 145:8; Joel 2:13

- slow to anger (BDB 74 CONSTRUCT BDB 60), cf. Exod. 34:6; Num. 14:18; Neh. 9:17;
Ps. 86:15; 103:8; 145:8; Joel 2:13

- abounding in lovingkindness (hesed, BDB 338, see
SPECIAL TOPIC: LOVINGKINDNESS), cf. Exod. 34:6;
Num. 14:18; Neh. 9:17; Ps. 86:15; 103:8; 145:8; Joel 2:13

- abounding in truth ("faithfulness," amen, BDB 54, see
SPECIAL TOPIC: BELIEVE, TRUST, FAITH AND FAITHFULNESS IN THE OT),
cf. Exod. 34:6; Ps. 86:15

- forgiving iniquity and transgression, cf. Num. 14:18

- will not (cf. Deut. 4:31)

- fail you

- destroy you

- forget the covenant with your fathers

- abundant forgiveness (BDB 699), cf. Neh. 9:17

- did not forsake them (BDB 736 I), cf. Neh. 9:17

- will not keep His anger forever, cf. Ps. 103:9

- relenting of evil, cf. Joel 2:13

Wow! What a wonderful God we trust, serve, and emulate!

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHARACTERISTICS OF ISRAEL'S GOD (OT)

verses.zh: 只要承认你的罪孽，就是你违背耶和华―你的　神，在各青翠树下向别神东奔西跑，没有听从我的话。这是耶和华说的。
verses.en: However, you must confess that you have done wrong[NOTE:1] and that you have rebelled against the Lord your God.You must confess[NOTE:2] that you have given yourself to[NOTE:3] foreign gods under every green treeand have not obeyed my commands,’ says the Lord.
notes: Heb “Only acknowledge your iniquity.”
The words “You must confess” are repeated to convey the connection. The Hebrew text has an introductory “that” in front of the second line and a coordinative “and” in front of the next two lines.

Heb “scattered your ways with foreign [gods]” or “spread out your breasts to strangers.”tc MT reads דְּרָכַיִךְ (derakhayikh, “your ways”), but the BHS editors suggest דּוֹדַיִךְ (dodayikh, “your breasts”) as an example of orthographic confusion. While the proposal makes sense, it remains a conjectural emendation since it is not supported by any actual manuscripts or ancient versions.
verses.commentary: 3:13-14 God's people must acknowledge their sin and turn back to faith and faithfulness in YHWH!

verses.zh: 耶和华说：背道的儿女啊，回来吧！因为我作你们的丈夫，并且我必将你们从一城取一人，从一族取两人，带到锡安。
verses.en: “Come back to me, my wayward sons,” says the Lord, “for I am your true master.[NOTE:1] If you do,[NOTE:2] I will take one of you from each town and two of you from each family group, and I will bring you back to Zion.
notes: Or “I am your true husband.”sn There is a wordplay between the term “true master” and the name of the pagan god Baal. The pronoun “I” is emphatic, creating a contrast between the Lord as Israel’s true master/husband versus Baal as Israel’s illegitimate lover/master. See 2:23-25.
The words “If you do” are not in the text but are implicit in the connection of the Hebrew verb with the preceding.
verses.commentary:
3:14 "I am a master to you" This is a play on the word Ba'al (BDB 127), the male fertility god of Canaan,
whose name means husband (cf. Jer. 31:32), master, lord, owner. This continues the family imagery.

For "sons" (BDB 119), see the same condemnation in Isa. 1:2-3.

verses.zh: 我也必将合我心的牧者赐给你们。他们必以知识和智慧牧养你们。」
verses.en: I will give you leaders[NOTE:1] who will be faithful to me.[NOTE:2] They will lead you with knowledge and insight.
notes: Heb “shepherds.”
Heb “after/according to my [own] heart.”
verses.commentary:
3:15 God's leaders (i.e. "shepherds," BDB 944), both civil and religious, will

- be after YHWH's own heart (BDB 524)

- feed the people with knowledge (BDB 395, only here in Jeremiah)

- feed the people with understanding (BDB 968, cf. Jer. 9:24)

Numbers 2 and 3 could refer to the shepherds themselves or what they give the people.

verses.zh: 耶和华说：「你们在国中生养众多；当那些日子，人必不再提说耶和华的约柜，不追想，不记念，不觉缺少，也不再制造。
verses.en: In those days, your population will greatly increase[NOTE:1] in the land. At that time,” says the Lord, “people will no longer talk about having the ark[NOTE:2] that contains the Lord’s covenant with us.[NOTE:3] They will not call it to mind, remember it, or miss it. No, that will not be done anymore![NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “you will become numerous and fruitful.”
Or “chest.”

Heb “the ark of the covenant.” It is called this because it contained the tables of the law, which in abbreviated form constituted their covenant obligations to the Lord (cf. Exod 31:18; 32:15; 34:29).
Or “Nor will another one be made”; Heb “one will not do/make [it?] again.”
verses.commentary:
3:16 "in those days" This refers to the New Covenant period (cf. Jer. 3:16-18; 31:31-34;
Ezek. 36:22-36) or the Messianic age.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MESSIANIC ERA

▣ "ark of the covenant" Whether it was actually missing at this point in time is
uncertain; this passage points to internal worship (cf. John 4:23; one wonders if Jesus had this text in mind when
He spoke to the woman at the well). There will be no need for a physical object representing YHWH. He Himself
will be among His people!

- it will not come to mind

- you will not rememer it

- you will not miss it

- you will not make a copy of it

The true hope of Israel was not in the temple (cf. Jer. 7; Acts 7), but in YHWH Himself. Ritual without faith
is a barrier to true biblical understanding of YHWH's plan of intimate fellowship with His unique creation (i.e. Gen. 1:26-27; 3:8).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE ARK OF THE COVENANT

verses.zh: 那时，人必称耶路撒冷为耶和华的宝座；万国必到耶路撒冷，在耶和华立名的地方聚集。他们必不再随从自己顽梗的恶心行事。
verses.en: At that time the city of Jerusalem[NOTE:1] will be called the Lord’s throne. All nations will gather there in Jerusalem to honor the Lord’s name.[NOTE:2] They will no longer follow the stubborn inclinations of their own evil hearts.[NOTE:3]
notes: For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
Heb “will gather to the name of the Lord.”
Heb “the stubbornness of their evil hearts.”
verses.commentary:
3:17 "Jerusalem" I think this refers to the New Jerusalem (i.e. the new people of God, cf. Rev. 21:1-4).
See my full notes in my new (2024) exegetical verse-by-verse commentary on Revelation.

▣ "all nations will be gathered to it" Notice the universal element (cf. Jer. 4:2; 12:15,16;
16:19; Isa. 2:2-4; 25:6-9; 45:22; 49:6; 54:4-5; 56:6-8; 60:3; 66:18,23). This would have shocked and
offended these Judean readers/hearers, just as Isaiah's inclusion of the nations shocked the
readers/hearers of his day!

It is always difficult to know if these passages refer to

- scattered exiles being brought home and rewarded by Gentiles

- Gentiles being fully welcomed into YHWH's covenant family

- The NT solves this issue by noting God's love for all humans.

- no more Jews and Gentiles, Rom. 2:28,29; 9:6; Gal. 3:7-9,29; 6:16; Eph. 2:11-3:13; 1 Pet. 3:6

- God's desire for all humans to be saved; see SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

SPECIAL TOPIC: WHY DO OT COVENANT
PROMISES SEEM SO DIFFERENT FROM NT COVENANT PROMISES?

▣ "nor will they walk any more after the stubbornness of their evil heart" This had been
the problem since Genesis 3 (see SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FALL OF MANKIND,
cf. Gen. 6:5,11,12; Jer. 11:8)! But the new day will reverse this self-centeredness. Compare Ezek. 18:31 with
Ezek. 36:26-27. The new covenant (Jer. 31:31-34) will be based on God's acts, not human acts!

The real question is to whom does "they" refer?

- the faithful remnant of Abraham's seed

- all of Abraham's seed alive in that day

- the Gentiles gathered to Jerusalem

For me, I have been deeply influenced by Rom. 2:28-29; Gal. 3:7-9,28; 6:16; Eph. 3:11-4:13;
1 Pet. 3:6. Abraham is the father of those who believe, not a racial/ethnic group.

SPECIAL TOPIC: STUBBORNNESS

verses.zh: 当那些日子，犹大家要和以色列家同行，从北方之地一同来到我赐给你们列祖为业之地。」
verses.en: At that time[NOTE:1] the nation of Judah and the nation of Israel will be reunited.[NOTE:2] Together they will come back from a land in the north to the land that I gave to your ancestors as a permanent possession.
notes: Heb “In those days.”
Heb “the house of Judah will walk together with the house of Israel.”
verses.commentary:
3:18 "the house of Judah. . .the house of Israel" The reunification of the thirteen tribes into one
nation would be the goal of much of Josiah's reform.

The "they" of v. 17 refers to the two nations which split in 922 B.C..

▣ "the land of the north" This is not a reference to a country to the north, but to the route
of return of the Jewish exiles (cf. Jer. 31:8).

▣ "to the land that I gave your fathers as an inheritance" See Gen. 12:1-3; 22:16-18;
Amos 9:15. YHWH acted toward this generation, and every generation of Abraham's seed, because of His
love and promises to the Patriarchs!

God has an eternal redemptive plan that involves Israel and the Messiah. His plan is
for all humanity. His plan will not be defeated, delayed, or destroyed!

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT PROMISES TO THE PATRIARCHS

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

verses.zh: 我说：我怎样将你安置在儿女之中，赐给你美地，就是万国中肥美的产业。我又说：你们必称我为父，也不再转去不跟从我。
verses.en: “I thought to myself,[NOTE:1] ‘Oh what a joy it would be for me to treat you like a son![NOTE:2] What a joy it would be for me to give[NOTE:3] you a pleasant land,the most beautiful piece of property there is in all the world!’[NOTE:4] I thought you would call me ‘Father’[NOTE:5] and would never cease being loyal to me.[NOTE:6]
notes: Heb “And I myself said.” See note on “I thought that she might come back to me” in 3:7.

Heb “How I would place you among the sons.” Israel appears to be addressed here contextually as the Lord’s wife (see the next verse). The pronouns of address in the first two lines are second feminine singular, as are the readings of the two verbs preferred by the Masoretes (the Qere readings) in the third and fourth lines. The verbs that are written in the text in the third and fourth lines (the Kethib readings) are second masculine plural, as is the verb describing Israel’s treachery in the next verse.sn The imagery here appears to be that of treating the wife as an equal heir with the sons and of giving her the best piece of property.
The words “What a joy it would be for me to” are not in the Hebrew text but are implied in the parallel structure.
Heb “the most beautiful heritage among the nations.”
Heb “my father.”
Heb “turn back from [following] after me.”
verses.commentary:
3:19 This verse begins a new strophe (i.e. Jer. 3:19-20). It could refer to

- the natural seed of Abraham (i.e. Israel as the firstborn son)

- the faith seed of Abraham (cf. Isa. 63:16; Rom. 2:28-29)

Jeremuah 3:20 implies option #1, while Jer. 3:19 implies option #2. Remember
Jer. 3:16-18 is describing the new age, the new covenant period.

The last two VERBS in Jer. 3:19 are PLURAL in the MT, but
the Masoretic scholars suggest a change to the SINGULAR.

The NET Bible (p. 1295) suggests (because of the gender of the VERBS)
that "Israel appears to be addressed here contextually as the Lord's wife" and
"the imagery here appears to be that of

- treating the wife as an equal heir with the sons

- giving her the best piece of property"

▣ "Father" See SPECIAL TOPIC: FATHERHOOD OF GOD

▣ "not turn away See
SPECIAL TOPIC: REPENTANCE (OT)

▣ 3:20 This refers to the early verses of this chapter.

verses.zh: 以色列家，你们向我行诡诈，真像妻子行诡诈离开她丈夫一样。这是耶和华说的。
verses.en: But, you have been unfaithful to me, nation of Israel,[NOTE:1] like an unfaithful wife who has left her husband,”[NOTE:2] says the Lord.
notes: Heb “house of Israel.”
Heb “a wife unfaithful from her husband.”

verses.zh: 在净光的高处听见人声，就是以色列人哭泣恳求之声，乃因他们走弯曲之道，忘记耶和华―他们的　神。
verses.en: “A noise is heard on the hilltops.It is the sound of the people of Israel crying and pleading to their gods.Indeed they have followed sinful ways;[NOTE:1] they have forgotten to be true to the Lord their God.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “A sound is heard on the hilltops, the weeping of the supplication of the children of Israel because [or indeed] they have perverted their way.” At issue here is whether the supplication is made to Yahweh in repentance because of what they have done or whether it is supplication to the pagan gods that is evidence of their perverted ways. The reference in this verse to the hilltops, where idolatry was practiced according to 3:2, and the reference to Israel’s unfaithfulness in the preceding verse make the latter more likely. For the asseverative use of the Hebrew particle (here rendered “indeed”) where the particle retains some of the explicative nuance, see BDB 472-73 s.v. כִּי 1.e and 3.c.
Heb “have forgotten the Lord their God.” But in view of the parallelism and the context, the word “forget” (like “know” and “remember”) involves more than mere intellectual activity.
verses.commentary:
3:21 "A voice" This would be the loud lament of Israel's repentance.

- weeping (BDB 113)

- supplications (BDB 337)

They are apparently calling out to their pagan gods (because of the first two lines of v. 22 and 3:2).

- perverting their way ‒ Hiphil PERFECT, BDB 730, KB 796

- forgetting YHWH ‒ Qal PERFECT, BDB 1013, KB 1489, cf. Jer. 2:32; 13:25

▣ "bare heights" This has been used sarcastically of the place of Ba'al worship (see note at v. 2),
but here it reflects a place of mourning (cf. Jdg. 11:37).

verses.zh: 你们这背道的儿女啊，回来吧！我要医治你们背道的病。看哪，我们来到你这里，因你是耶和华―我们的　神。
verses.en: Come back to me, you wayward people.I want to cure your waywardness.[NOTE:1] Say,[NOTE:2] ‘Here we are. We come to youbecause you are the Lord our God.
notes: Or “I will forgive your apostasies.” Heb “I will [or want to] heal your apostasies.” For the use of the verb “heal” (רָפָא, rafaʾ) to refer to spiritual healing and forgiveness, see Hos 14:4.

Or “They say.” There is an obvious ellipsis of a verb of saying here since the preceding words are those of the Lord and the following are those of the people. However, there is debate about whether the people’s words are a response to the Lord’s invitation, a response which is said to be inadequate according to the continuation in 4:1-4, or whether they are the Lord’s model for Israel’s confession of repentance, to which 4:1-4 adds further instructions about the proper heart attitude that should accompany it. The former implies a dialogue with an unmarked, twofold shift in speaker between 3:22b-25 and 4:1-4, while the latter assumes the same main speaker throughout, with an unmarked instruction only in 3:22b-25. The latter disrupts the flow of the passage less and appears more likely.
verses.commentary:
3:22-23 These verses have words from

- YHWH

- return faithless sons ‒ Qal IMPERFECT

- I will heal your faithlessness ‒ Qal IMPERATIVE

- the faithless sons

- we come to You ‒ Qal PERFECT

- for You are the Lord our God

- the hills (i.e. a place of fertility worship) are a deception

- salvation is only in YHWH

Jer. 3:25 continues the words of "the faithless sons" (i.e. their
repentance)

- let us lie down in our shame ‒ Qal COHORTATIVE

- let our humiliation cover us ‒ Piel IMPERFECT used in
a JUSSIVE sense

- we have sinned against the Lord our God ‒ Qal
PERFECT

- we and our fathers have sinned since our youth even to this day (cf. Jer. 22:21)

- we have not obeyed the voice of the Lord our God

3:22 The UBS Handbook notes that the words

- return (BDB 996, KB 1427)

- faithless (BDB 1000)

- faithlessness (BDB 1000)

all are based on the same Hebrew consonants, שׁוב (p. 113). Sound
plays are very common in Hebrew poetry.

▣ "I will heal your faithlessness" Here, like Ps. 103:3; Isa. 53:4-5; Hosea 14:4, this
imagery refers to spiritual healing (i.e. the forgiveness of sin).

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEALING

verses.zh: 仰望从小山或从大山的喧嚷中得帮助，真是枉然的。以色列得救，诚然在乎耶和华―我们的　神。
verses.en: We know our noisy worship of false gods on the hills and mountains did not help us.[NOTE:1] We know that the Lord our God is the only one who can deliver Israel.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “Truly in vain from the hills the noise/commotion [and from] the mountains.” The syntax of the Hebrew sentence is very elliptical here.
Heb “Truly in the Lord our God is deliverance for Israel.”
verses.commentary:
3:23 "surely" The ADVERB (BDB 38) occurs twice and gives the words of the
people a solemnity!

▣ Lines one and two of verse 23 are depicting Ba'al worship on the mountains of
Israel. These worship scenes may be noisy but they cannot save; only YHWH can save (line four).

verses.zh: 从我们幼年以来，那可耻的偶像将我们列祖所劳碌得来的羊群、牛群，和他们的儿女都吞吃了。
verses.en: From earliest times our worship of that shameful god, Baal, has taken away[NOTE:1] all that our ancestors[NOTE:2] worked for.It has taken away our flocks and our herdsand even our sons and daughters.
notes: Heb “From our youth the shameful thing has eaten up….” The shameful thing is specifically identified as Baal in Jer 11:13. Compare also the shift in certain names such as Ishbaal (“man of Baal”) to Ishbosheth (“man of shame”).
Heb “fathers” (also in v. 25).
verses.commentary:
3:24 "shameful thing" This is used sarcastically of Ba'al (cf. Jer. 11:13; Hosea 9:10) or
because of the mention of "sons and daughters," it may refer to the worship of Molech.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MOLECH.

verses.zh: 我们在羞耻中躺卧吧！愿惭愧将我们遮盖；因为从立国（原文是幼年）以来，我们和我们的列祖常常得罪耶和华―我们的　神，没有听从耶和华―我们　神的话。
verses.en: Let us acknowledge[NOTE:1] our shame.Let us bear the disgrace that we deserve.[NOTE:2] For we have sinned against the Lord our God,both we and our ancestors.From earliest times to this very daywe have not obeyed the Lord our God.’
notes: Heb “Let us lie down in….”
Heb “Let us be covered with disgrace.”
verses.commentary:
3:25 "from our youth even to this day" This rebellion was no new or passing thing. It went back
to the wilderness wandering period (i.e. Exodus 32).

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own
interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.
You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of
the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- To what is Jeremiah comparing God's people?

- What two metaphors does he use of God?

- Did His people truly repent? Why or why not?

- Does Jer. 3:19-25 reflect the future or post-exilic time?

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which
means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the
light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not
relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare
your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is
the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every
paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- Jeremiah 2:1-4:4 forms a literary unit. Identifying literary units is crucial for contextual interpretations. See
Introduction, VII.

- Jeremiah 3 is a word play on the word shub (שׁוב, BDB 996, KB 1427), which
means "to turn," either to something or to someone. The term is used in both religious and non-religious senses.
But, its main theological emphasis is a turning from evil and turning to YHWH (cf. Jer. 3:7,10,14; 8:4,6; 18:8;
26:3; 31:19; 44:5).

SPECIAL TOPIC: REPENTANCE (OT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: Seek the Lord

- The broken covenant is illustrated as a broken marriage resulting in a legal divorce. However,
YHWH's grace is so powerful that the Deut. 24:1-4 requirements are annulled (i.e. faithless,
idolatrous Israel can return to her first husband, YHWH, v. 1)!

Israel was almost never faithful to the Sinai covenant. She had such few godly
kings. It is surely possible that

- YHWH's intent was to use His blessing on Israel to attract the nations, but, they were never faithful
and the curses of Lev. 26 and Deut. 28 became a reality.

SPECIAL TOPIC: STUBBORNNESS (OT)

- YHWH used Israel, with all of her special blessings (cf. Rom. 9:4-5), to clearly demonstrate that
fallen mankind (see SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FALL OF MANKIND) could never
keep the Mosaic Covenant (see SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP and
SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT). Therefore, a new covenant
based on YHWH's actions was required (cf. Jer. 31:31-34; Ezek. 36:22-36). The key was YHWH's "grace"
and "mercy" (see SPECIAL TOPIC: CHARACTERISTICS OF ISRAEL'S GOD)
and not human performance!

The covenant with Israel was a crucial, but temporary, way (cf. Matt. 5:17-19) to demonstrate
YHWH's plan for the salvation and restoration to Edenic fellowship.

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMTIVE PLAN
